name: TESSERA Corponation Neural Severance Rod NSR-1 'Blackout'
description:
The NSR-1 'Blackout' occupies a unique and deeply controversial niche in Meridian's weapons market: it is designed not to shock the human body, but to destroy the electronics within it. Rather than a high-voltage arc, the Blackout generates a precisely shaped electromagnetic pulse upon contact — a localized, directed EMP burst calibrated to induce damaging voltage spikes in the frequency range used by virtually all commercial BCI hardware, cyberware control units, augmentation power buses, and synthetic neural substrates. Physical sensation upon contact is minimal — a mild warmth and a brief disorientation — but the aftermath is catastrophic for augmented individuals. A direct contact EMP burst from the NSR-1 has been documented to permanently disable BCI units, fuse cyberware actuators, wipe non-shielded neural memory storage, and in the case of individuals with cardiac or respiratory augmentation, trigger life-threatening device failure.

TESSERA developed the NSR-1 ostensibly as a 'counter-augmentation security tool' for use in corporate espionage scenarios and executive protection — the logic being that a heavily augmented corporate operative represents a threat profile that standard weapons cannot adequately address. The weapon is marketed with clinical precision: its product literature does not use words like 'shock' or 'pain' but instead describes 'selective electronic neutralization' and 'augmentation countermeasures.' This sanitized framing has done little to prevent the weapon from being regarded, in both legal and street contexts, as one of the most feared melee weapons in Meridian.

The NSR-1's legality is a patchwork nightmare. The device produces no projectile, no explosive, and no conventional lethal force against unaugmented individuals; Meridian's weapons statutes were largely written before widespread augmentation and contain significant gaps around EMP-class devices. TESSERA has exploited these gaps aggressively, maintaining that the NSR-1 is a 'security technology device' rather than a weapon. Augmentation rights advocacy groups have pushed for specific legislation criminalizing anti-cyberware weaponry as a form of targeted disability violence, with limited legislative success to date.
legality: Restricted — classified as electronic countermeasure device rather than weapon under current Meridian statute; sale requires TESSERA authorized dealer registration; use against individuals with life-sustaining augmentation constitutes aggravated assault under case law precedent
specifications:
Length: 55 cm
Weight: 0.8 kg
Pulse Type: Directed contact EMP
Pulse Frequency Range: 0.1 MHz – 40 GHz (covers all known commercial cyberware bands)
Effective Contact Radius: 8 cm from strike point
Operator Shielding: TESSERA FaradaCore grip (full EMP isolation)
Power Cell: TESSERA NanoCell T-7
Battery Life: 120 pulses per cell
Augmentation Damage Rating: Severe (commercial grade); Moderate (military-shielded)
Physical Trauma to Unaugmented Target: Negligible
Body: Carbon-fiber composite, matte black
tactical_use: The NSR-1 is used primarily in two contexts: corporate security details protecting executives against augmented threats, and — less officially — by those seeking to strip augmented individuals of their capabilities before or during a confrontation. A single contact strike to the head or torso of an individual with an active BCI will typically render the BCI non-functional within seconds; a strike to a limb with cyberware actuators will cause the affected limb to seize or go limp. Operators are trained to follow an NSR-1 strike with physical restraint, as the target's disorientation window is brief and the device does not induce unconsciousness in unaugmented individuals.
cultural_context: The Blackout is called 'the Eraser' in Tier 1 and 2 slang, and its reputation carries a specific existential dread that ordinary shock weapons do not. For individuals whose augmentation is medical — limb replacements, cardiac regulators, vision systems — being struck by an Eraser is not merely an assault but a potential permanent disability event. The weapon has become a symbol in augmentation rights discourse, representing the weaponization of people's dependence on their own bodies. Among corporate security professionals, carrying one is a statement about the threat environment: it signals that you work in circles where your adversaries are heavily wired and you've planned for that.
known_users: TESSERA corporate security and executive protection details
black market — sold to those targeting augmented individuals
story_hooks: A prominent augmentation rights lawyer is found catatonic in her Tier 4 office — her BCI, which also managed treatment for a degenerative neurological condition, has been fried. Security footage shows a visitor carrying what appears to be a standard corporate umbrella. The lawyer had been building a class action against TESSERA. The visiting attorney's firm is a TESSERA legal subsidiary.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, purposeful baton with an almost clinical aesthetic. The NSR-1 reads as a precision instrument rather than a traditional weapon — its form factor suggests corporate R&D more than street violence. The shaft tapers slightly toward a weighted contact head, and the grip is noticeably distinct from the rest of the body, suggesting deliberate operator isolation.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 55 cm (21.6 inches). Shaft diameter: 2.2 cm tapering to 2.8 cm at contact head. Grip section: 12 cm with subtle ergonomic swelling.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and deceptively light at 0.8 kg — the carbon-fiber construction makes it feel almost fragile in hand, belying its lethal electronic payload. Grip-heavy design ensures the operator's hand stays in the shielded zone.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber composite body with integrated conductive pathways. Contact head features tungsten-alloy strike surface. Grip wrapped in proprietary TESSERA FaradaCore shielding — a woven metallic-polymer blend.
physical_description.finish: Matte black DLC (diamond-like carbon) coating across the shaft, reducing reflectivity and giving a non-tactical, almost medical appearance. The grip section has a subtly textured finish for traction.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black primary with gunmetal gray accents where the conductive pathways are exposed near the contact head. Minimal branding — TESSERA lettering in small, raised sans-serif on the grip.
physical_description.grip_texture: Densely woven FaradaCore material with fine crosshatch pattern — grip feels technical and slightly cool to the touch, almost like holding a piece of laboratory equipment. No rubberization; the material is proprietary and slightly resistant to sweat.
distinctive_features: Subtle LED status indicator (blue when charged, amber when drained) recessed into the grip near the pommel
Thin conductive pathways etched visibly along the shaft, running toward the contact head like circuit traces
Contact head features a slightly domed, slightly darkened tungsten surface — distinctive from the rest of the matte finish
Barely-visible seam line where the shielded grip section joins the main shaft
Small, recessed power cell access port on the grip underside
Faint geometric etching on the grip — possibly intentional branding or grip texture enhancement
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA CORPONATION logo (geometric Φ-inspired mark) embossed subtly on the grip above the hand position. Model designation 'NSR-1' and serial number plate on the underside. No explicit 'Blackout' branding visible — the name exists only in marketing materials and street parlance.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show minimal wear — the matte finish hides scuffs well. Well-maintained corporate security units show no scratches. Used units may have micro-fractures in the FaradaCore grip from repeated use or field impacts, but the weapon's electronic internals remain hidden and pristine. Street-worn examples might show grip degradation and loss of the distinctive sheen on the contact head.
